correctness.rationale: For B=[[4,1/2],[1,1/4]], recovery/break/creation constants one, stationary links give K=[[4,1/2],[1/2,1/4]], ρ(K)=(17+sqrt(241))/8>1. At any nonzero equilibrium y1>=3/4 makes q(y1)=[max(0,1-2y1)]² vanish; z21=0 and group2 equation forces y2=0, y1=3/4. For positive creation, continuous stationary contact fractions Z_ij(y)>0, Perron left-weighted local T(y)>y growth, Brouwer perturbation Tη and graph irreducibility produce strictly positive fixed point. The IFT at boundary Jacobian [[-3,1/8],[0,-3/4]] gives derivative (1/24,1). Exact independent algebra checked K, eigenvalues and IFT derivative. No stability/uniqueness claim.

originality.rationale: Achterberg–Sensi–Sottile (Chaos 2025) conjecture R0>1 implies fully endemic equilibrium under their nonnegative contact-creation framework. The explicit zero-creation counterexample falsifies that unrestricted conjecture but not their stronger minimum-row-sum Theorem 5 (here min sum=3/4). The positive-creation Perron–Brouwer theorem specifies a meaningful sufficient condition absent from their statement. Single-group and different state-dependent SIS models are inapplicable.
residual_risks: Existence conclusion is not a stability/uniqueness/global persistence theorem; boundaries c>0 must hold on entire closed prevalence cube.
Some later unindexed follow-up to Conjecture 6 could independently identify the same counterexample; historical priority remains best-of-knowledge.

final_claim: In adaptive multigroup SIS networks with nonnegative, possibly vanishing contact creation, R0>1 need not yield any fully positive endemic equilibrium (explicit 2-group counterexample); with irreducible infection graph and strictly positive creation on each existing edge for all prevalence values, R0>1 does ensure a fully endemic equilibrium, and restoring creation η in the counterexample makes y2=η+O(η²).
limitations: Counterexample uses C1 zero-capable nonincreasing creation q; positive-creation theorem guarantees existence only, not stability or persistence; η expansion is local.
Existence conclusion is not a stability/uniqueness/global persistence theorem; boundaries c>0 must hold on entire closed prevalence cube.
Some later unindexed follow-up to Conjecture 6 could independently identify the same counterexample; historical priority remains best-of-knowledge.
